name: Fortuynism
summary: Fortuynism is the political outlook of the Dutch sociologist and politician Pim Fortuyn and his list in 2002: a mix of liberalism, populism and nationalism. It combines a business-like, small-scale and accountable public sector, an attack on the closed regent culture and consensus politics of the Purple coalitions, and strict limits on immigration with a demand that newcomers integrate into liberal Dutch values, defended through gay and women's rights and sharp criticism of fundamentalist Islam.
scope: Represents Pim Fortuyn's ideas as set out in the LPF election programme Zakelijk met een hart (2002) and as described by Lucardie and Voerman (2002), who trace them to liberalism, populism and nationalism, by Lucardie's chapter in Twenty-First Century Populism (2008), who calls it an eclectic mix of liberalism, nationalism, communitarianism and moderate populism, and by Houtman, Achterberg and Kemmers (2012). Fortuyn's own books were read only through these. It excludes later parties that claimed his legacy (LPF after 2002, Wilders' PVV) and the broader family of right-wing populism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fortuyn's 'modernised liberalism' keeps the state out of a modern open economy beyond managing the public sector, and the programme wants farmers and entrepreneurs to produce in a healthy market, though it declines to privatise service monopolies.

cut-welfare.rationale: The programme stops inflow into the WAO disability scheme by limiting it to work-related illness and abolishes income-dependent subsidies that create the poverty trap.

empower-police-military.rationale: The programme puts more police on the street, expands cell capacity and gives the Marechaussee police powers and strengthens customs, while keeping the army at strength but trimming its missions.

decide-locally.rationale: The programme says responsibilities must be placed as low in the administrative structure as possible and that scale enlargement must be reversed to bring government close to the citizen; Lucardie calls 'small is beautiful' central.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The programme gives all citizens the same rights and duties regardless of sexual orientation, and Houtman documents Fortuyn's defence of gay emancipation as a great modern achievement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The programme says preserving the existing Dutch culture in all its forms is of great importance, and Houtman records Fortuyn's defence of Dutch identity against cultural relativism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The programme says plainly that the Netherlands is not an immigration country and that immigration must be resisted to the maximum.

open-borders.rationale: The programme declares the Netherlands not an immigration country and demands maximum resistance to immigration and a halt to yearly inflows.

central-planning.rationale: Fortuyn held that the state should not intervene in a modern open economy; he had given up Marxism and other socialism.

unions-good.rationale: In Fortuyn's contract society wage-earners negotiate directly rather than rely on trade unions, and the programme calls for extreme restraint in real wage rises.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Fortuyn wanted wage-earners to negotiate pensions and disability cover directly with employers instead of through unions, and the programme puts the poldermodel under critical review.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Oudenampsen traces Fortuyn's critique of the establishment to a neoliberal critique of the Dutch corporatist welfare state; the programme calls the poldermodel stalled and the wage-price spiral to be broken.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: Houtman records Fortuyn's contempt for the closed consensus culture of the Poldermodel and the programme puts the poldermodel under critical review.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Lucardie reports that Fortuyn believed drugs should be legalised.

rehabilitation.rationale: Lucardie says Fortuyn favoured repression over prevention and social reform against crime, and the programme expands cells for repeat offenders.

state-harmful.rationale: The programme assigns the state real tasks (quality and access of care, police, defence, culture) and Fortuyn wanted to restore democracy, not abolish the state.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programme has the government guard the quality and accessibility of health care, run police and defence, and fund culture, well beyond a night-watchman role.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme bases tax and premium burdens on the solidarity principle, with the strongest shoulders bearing the heaviest burden.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme says the strongest shoulders will bear the heaviest burdens, which is progressive rather than flat.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programme strengthens the police, Marechaussee, customs and army as state tasks.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The programme demands more police on the street and more cell capacity with staff.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme calls the maintenance of the army important and keeps its fighting strength and traditions.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The programme demands clear quality and quantity criteria and frequent accounting for results, from health care to police leadership, under the motto 'businesslike, but with a heart'.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The programme gives private care institutions the same rights as regular hospitals while the government guards quality and accessibility.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Lucardie says Fortuyn favoured assimilation of immigrants into Dutch culture; the programme demands full effort from minorities and fights practices incompatible with emancipation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The programme says all citizens have the same rights and duties regardless of race, sex, faith and orientation.

separate-church-state.rationale: The programme states that church and state are separated in the Netherlands, 'so also mosque and state'.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme credits the separation of executive, legislative and judicial powers with letting citizens develop in relative freedom and calls for protecting that freedom.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Houtman records Fortuyn calling Islam a backward culture and wanting to admit no more Muslim immigrants, but the programme itself targets fundamentalist discrimination of women, so the line is mixed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The programme keeps the monarchy beyond discussion with a ceremonial and unifying function for the head of state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The programme says the monarchy is not up for discussion.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The programme retains the (hereditary) Dutch monarchy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The programme keeps the hereditary monarchy, so hereditary titles and privileges are not to be abolished across the board.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state remains the monarch; only mayors and the prime minister are to be elected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The head of state keeps only a ceremonial and unifying role, so he does not command the forces or choose ministers.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: The programme leaves the head of state a ceremonial, unifying function only.

direct-votes.rationale: The programme wants a binding referendum on new EU members and more direct citizen involvement, but Lucardie says Fortuyn showed no enthusiasm for direct democracy and wanted politicians to lead.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme wants citizens involved more directly in governing, while Lucardie says Fortuyn showed no enthusiasm for direct democracy.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The programme supports the EU as a great contribution to peace but with retained identity and, where possible, sovereignty, and Fortuyn opposed a federal Europe.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The programme attacks a self-satisfied political culture of appointed regents and Houtman documents Fortuyn's charge that elites dodge responsibility; corruption in the strict sense is not charged.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The programme continues the policy of building ownership by selling rental homes.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The programme says the Zalm norm on budget discipline must be kept without exception.

price-stability-first.rationale: The programme lists inflation among the failures of the Purple coalition and demands that it be fought with force.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The programme wants the tax system cleared of burdens such as too-high VAT.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The programme lists the ecotax among the inflationary taxes to be cleared and rejects environmental tax measures without analysis.

conscription.rationale: The programme asks to examine social and military service for boys and girls from eighteen, and Lucardie calls it Fortuyn's proposal of universal service.

equal-conscription.rationale: The programme proposes examining service for boys and girls alike.

avoid-permanent-military-alliances.rationale: The programme accepts the Netherlands' role as a NATO partner.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The programme keeps the Dutch army and its NATO partnership.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The programme accepts the Netherlands' NATO partnership.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The programme says all citizens have the same rights and duties regardless of faith.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal rights regardless of sex is stated in the programme, and Lucardie calls Fortuyn a strong advocate of equality irrespective of gender.

women-must-cover.rationale: The programme calls discrimination against women in fundamentalist Islamic circles unacceptable and gives all citizens equal rights regardless of sex and faith.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Equal rights regardless of faith and separation of mosque and state leave no room for punishing apostasy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Separation of church and mosque from the state and equal rights regardless of faith exclude punishing blasphemy.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The programme gives all citizens equal rights regardless of sexual orientation, and Fortuyn defended gay emancipation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The programme separates church and mosque from the state.

clerical-rule.rationale: The programme separates church and mosque from the state in a democratic society.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Equal rights regardless of faith and separation of religion and state leave no basis for restricting conversion.

national-church-status.rationale: The programme separates church and state and gives citizens equal rights regardless of faith.

religious-nation.rationale: The programme treats all citizens as equal regardless of faith, so the nation is not defined by religion.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Equal rights regardless of faith exclude legal limits on marriage between religions.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The programme gives all citizens the same rights and duties regardless of race.

racial-franchise.rationale: The programme gives all citizens the same rights regardless of race, and Lucardie notes Fortuyn was not an ethnic nationalist.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme gives all citizens the same rights and duties regardless of sex.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Equal rights regardless of sex in the programme leave no room for husbandly authority.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The programme gives all citizens equal rights regardless of sex.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The programme gives all citizens equal rights regardless of sex.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The programme gives all citizens equal rights regardless of sexual orientation.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Lucardie, following Akkerman, calls Fortuyn a liberal nationalist, not an ethnic or ethnocratic one, and the programme asks for integration, not ethnic homogeneity.

population-transfer.rationale: The programme gives all citizens equal rights and aims at integration and emancipation of minorities, not their removal.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The programme gives all citizens equal rights regardless of race and aims at integrating minorities.

native-born-offices.rationale: The programme gives all citizens the same rights and duties, and Lucardie notes the LPF list included non-white immigrants.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The programme works through the justice system and the separation of powers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The programme calls preserving the existing culture in all its forms of great importance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The programme says many immigrants come from countries without the Judeo-Christian-humanist development, and Houtman records Fortuyn's rejection of cultural relativism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Houtman records Fortuyn's attack on a self-renewing meritocratic elite of professionals and his stress on accountable administrators.

one-party-rule.rationale: The programme and Lucardie describe a democratic project, with separated powers and elected officials.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Fortuyn gave up Marxism and defended separated powers and democracy.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme defends hard-won freedoms and separated powers.

party-controls-media.rationale: The programme defends hard-won freedoms and separated powers.

party-commands-army.rationale: The programme keeps the army under the state with separated powers.

total-state.rationale: Fortuyn favoured a state that stays out of the open economy and the programme deregulates schools, care and farming.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Lucardie describes Fortuyn's contract society in which wage-earners negotiate as entrepreneurs of their own labour.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Fortuyn's contract society keeps wage-earners negotiating pay as entrepreneurs of their own labour.

democracy-best.rationale: Lucardie says Fortuyn's ambition was to restore democracy and give power back to the people.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme backs ICT with auction money but Lucardie says the state should not intervene in the open economy; no position on directing investment.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: Houtman quotes Fortuyn saying he would admit no more Muslims if legally possible and the programme ties integration problems to immigrants from outside the Judeo-Christian-humanist tradition.

missingStatements.text: Heads of government should be elected directly by the people.
missingStatements.rationale: The programme demands that the mayor and the prime minister be elected, and Lucardie reports that Fortuyn wanted such public officials elected directly by the people.

quotes.text: De burgemeester en de minister-president dienen te worden gekozen.
public officials like mayors and the prime minister should be elected directly by the people.
quotes.where: Lucardie, The Netherlands, p159, section The political project

notes: Sources are the 2002 LPF programme (nine pages), Lucardie's 2008 chapter, Houtman et al. 2012, and two abstract-only records; Fortuyn's own books were not obtained. The programme and Fortuyn's own words differ on Islam (programme targets fundamentalism, Fortuyn called Islam a backward culture), marked low. Many answers on religion, race, sex and regime form follow from the programme's statement of equal rights regardless of race, sex, faith and orientation, and from its separation of church and state and of powers; they are medium. Themes searched in the saved sources: economy and tax, welfare, crime, immigration, EU, defence, government structure, culture, environment (nothing stated), technology, world affairs. Nothing stated on climate, nuclear power, abortion, drugs beyond Lucardie's remark, or foreign intervention, so those stay null. The LPF's brief time in government (2002) is not treated as a record.
